title: Calendar View for Tasks - Full Implementation
description: Complete implementation of month/week calendar views for task scheduling with drag-drop rescheduling, filtering integration, and responsive design. Epic tracks all phases from foundation through testing and optimization.

title: Phase 1: Foundation - Calendar Component Architecture
description:
Create the foundation components and hooks for calendar view:

## Tasks:
- Create CalendarView.tsx: Main container with month/week toggle
- Create MonthCalendarGrid.tsx: Month grid rendering
- Create CalendarDayCell.tsx: Single day cell with task preview
- Create useCalendarState.ts: Custom hook for calendar state management
- Update TaskPage.tsx to add 'calendar' view mode option
- Update useTaskPageSettings.ts to support calendar state
- Wire up existing TaskContext and filtering integration

## Success Criteria:
- Month view renders grid correctly
- Tasks display as badges in cells (max 3 inline)
- "+N more" badge shows overflow count
- Day cells are interactive (click state)
- View mode switcher works (list/kanban/matrix/calendar)
- Preferences persist to localStorage

title: Create CalendarView.tsx + useCalendarState.ts
description:
Build the main container component and calendar state management hook.

## Deliverables:
- CalendarView.tsx: Main component handling month/week toggle
  - Props: tasks, filters, viewMode
  - State: selectedDate, view ('month'|'week'), sidebar visibility
  - Renders appropriate view (MonthCalendarGrid or WeekCalendarView)
  
- useCalendarState.ts: Custom hook
  - useState: selectedDate, calendarMode, sidebarOpen
  - useMemo: groupTasksByDate() for month view
  - Helper: navigateMonth(direction), setToday()
  - Exports: state object with memoized selectors

## Integration:
- Consume from TaskContext
- Use useTaskPageSettings for persistence
- Connect to useTaskFiltering for filtered tasks

## Tests:
- Hook renders without errors
- Navigation changes selectedDate
- Grouping memoized correctly
- State persists across renders

title: Create MonthCalendarGrid.tsx + CalendarDayCell.tsx
description:
Build the visual month grid and individual day cells.

## Deliverables:
- MonthCalendarGrid.tsx: Main month grid
  - Uses react-calendar base grid
  - 7-column layout (Sun-Sat)
  - Current day highlighted
  - Previous/next month dates dimmed
  - Callback: onDayClick(date)
  
- CalendarDayCell.tsx: Single day cell
  - Props: date, tasks, isSelected, onDayClick
  - Display logic: sort tasks by priority, show max 3
  - Badge rendering: task title, priority color, status icon
  - Overflow: +N more badge with task count
  - Styling: grid cell, task badges, hover states

## Styling:
- Tailwind CSS grid layout
- Color-coded by status (todo, in_progress, done)
- Responsive: scales to container width
- Touch-friendly: 48px minimum cell height

## Tests:
- Grid renders correct number of days
- Day click handler called with correct date
- Overflow handling: ≤3 show inline, 4+ show badge
- Color assignment matches status

title: Integrate calendar into TaskPage + update view settings
description:
Wire the calendar view into the main tasks page and persist settings.

## Changes:
- TaskPage.tsx:
  - Add 'calendar' to View Mode select dropdown
  - Conditionally render <CalendarView /> when viewMode === 'calendar'
  - Pass context + filtering props to CalendarView
  
- useTaskPageSettings.ts:
  - Extend viewMode union: 'list' | 'kanban' | 'matrix' | 'calendar'
  - Add calendarViewMode state: 'month' | 'week'
  - Add selectedCalendarDate state: Date | null
  - Persist all to localStorage

## Testing:
- View mode switcher includes calendar option
- Calendar renders when selected
- Settings persist across page refresh
- Switching back to list view works
- No console errors

title: Wire up existing filtering + TaskContext
description:
Connect calendar to live task data and filtering system.

## Integration:
- CalendarView receives filtered tasks from useTaskFiltering
- Respects all existing filters:
  - dateView filter (today/tomorrow/all → filtered on calendar)
  - Search text (applies to task display)
  - Tag filters (💡 = colored badges on tasks)
  - Priority filters
  - Show/hide completed toggle
  
- Data flow:
  - TaskContext.tasks → useTaskFiltering → CalendarView
  - Grouping by scheduled_date happens in useCalendarState
  - Any filter change triggers re-render
  
## Testing:
- Filter changes update calendar immediately
- Tag click filters calendar tasks
- Search narrows task display
- Show completed toggle works
- No duplicates or missing tasks
- Performance acceptable with hundreds of tasks

title: Phase 2: User Interactions - Day Selection & Task Management
description:
Implement interactive features for the month view:

## Tasks:
- Create CalendarSidebar.tsx: Right panel showing selected day's tasks
- Implement day click handler → open sidebar with task list
- Implement task click → open existing TaskDialog
- Create CalendarNavigationBar.tsx: Month/year selector and today button
- Add filter integration (tag click, search, show completed toggle)
- Implement create task quick action (right-click context menu)
- Add keyboard navigation (arrow keys between months/weeks)

## Success Criteria:
- Click day opens sidebar with all tasks for that date
- Click task in sidebar opens TaskDialog (existing component)
- Navigation controls work (prev/next month, today)
- Tag filters apply to calendar display
- Search narrows calendar tasks
- Show/hide completed toggle works
- Create task pre-fills with selected date
- Keyboard shortcuts work (Shift+Today, arrow navigation)

title: Phase 3: Drag-Drop Rescheduling
description:
Implement drag-and-drop to reschedule tasks between dates:

## Tasks:
- Integrate @hello-pangea/dnd library (already in dependencies)
- Create drag-drop handlers for month view cells
- Implement drop handler: update task scheduled_date via API
- Call saveExistingTask() with updated date
- Implement optimistic UI update + rollback on error
- Add visual feedback during drag (highlight drop zones)
- Handle edge cases: dragging across months, same-day re-order
- Test mobile: long-press context menu alternative

## Success Criteria:
- Drag task within same month works
- Drag task across months advances calendar view
- Drop updates task immediately (optimistic)
- Error state shows toast and reverts task position
- Visual feedback clear (drag zone highlights)
- Mobile long-press provides alternative interaction
- No duplicate drag handlers or memory leaks

title: Phase 4: Week View & Responsive Polish
description:
Implement week view and optimize for all screen sizes:

## Tasks:
- Create WeekCalendarView.tsx: Week view with 7-column layout
- Implement all-day task section at top
- Create week navigation (prev/next week, today)
- Add week/month view toggle in CalendarNavigationBar
- Responsive breakpoints: mobile (week only), tablet (week default), desktop (month default)
- Visual polish: color scheme, spacing, typography alignment
- Accessibility audit: focus indicators, ARIA labels, color contrast
- Mobile optimizations: touch targets (48px minimum), simplified layout

## Success Criteria:
- Week view displays Mon-Sun in columns
- Tasks group by day with all-day section
- Mobile: calendar readable and accessible
- Tablet+: Month view preferred, week available
- No color-only distinctions (add icons/patterns)
- Full keyboard accessibility (Tab, Enter, Arrow keys)
- ARIA labels on all interactive elements
- Dark mode compatible

title: Phase 5: Testing, Performance & Launch
description:
Comprehensive testing and optimization:

## Unit Tests:
- Date utilities: calendar computation, week boundaries, month transitions
- Component logic: task grouping, overflow detection, color assignment
- Filtering: date range queries, tag/search integration

## Integration Tests:
- TaskContext → CalendarView data flow
- Filter updates propagate correctly
- Drag-drop API sync and refresh
- Task dialog opens with correct ID
- View mode switching preserves state

## Edge Cases & Regression:
- Month/year boundaries (Jan 31 → Feb 1, Dec 31 → Jan 1)
- Daylight saving time transitions
- Timezone edge cases (midnight boundaries)
- Large datasets (1000+ tasks)
- Completed tasks mixed with active

## Performance & QA:
- Profile calendar render with 1000+ tasks (<200ms)
- Drag-drop UI feedback <50ms
- Filter updates <300ms
- No memory leaks (DevTools profiler)
- Lighthouse performance audit
- Cross-browser testing (Chrome, Firefox, Safari)
- Mobile device testing (iOS, Android)

## Success Criteria:
- All unit tests passing (80%+ coverage)
- All integration tests passing
- No regressions in existing features
- Performance benchmarks met
- Zero console errors/warnings
- Accessible on WCAG AA level
- Ready for production deployment

title: Add calendar view for tasks
description:
# Calendar View for Tasks

## Goal
Add a calendar view option to the TaskPage to display tasks on their scheduled dates.

## Current State
- Tasks support ScheduledDate, DueDate, and ReminderTime fields
- Frontend has multiple view modes: list view, Kanban board, and Eisenhower matrix
- Date filtering exists (today/tomorrow/all) but no visual calendar representation
- Timezone handling is already in place

## Planning Tasks
1. **Decide UI approach**: Month view, week view, or both?
2. **Design calendar component**: Determine how tasks appear on dates
3. **Handle task-to-date mapping**: Logic for scheduling multiple tasks on same date
4. **Implement backend changes** (if needed): Current API might already support calendar queries
5. **Frontend calendar component**: React component library choice and implementation
6. **Integrate with existing features**: Tag filtering, task selection, create/edit flows must work
7. **Responsive design**: Mobile calendar view
8. **Testing**: Calendar rendering, date filtering edge cases

title: Backend maintainability cleanup (entrypoint: go-backend/main.go)
description:
Comprehensive review + cleanup plan starting from go-backend/main.go.

Focus areas:
- configuration/env var loading
- logging + server lifecycle (startup/shutdown)
- dependency initialization (DB, S3, Mail, Stripe, Typesense, LLM)
- routing organization + middleware/auth stack
- background goroutines/async init + error handling

Non-goals:
- changing API behavior/contracts
- adding new infrastructure or major new dependencies

acceptance_criteria: - Review beads for each focus area are completed with concrete recommendations and file pointers\n- Follow-up implementation beads are created/updated from the recommendations\n- No behavior changes introduced during the review phase

title: Review: configuration + env var management
description:
Inventory environment variables referenced by go-backend/main.go and related bootstrap code. Evaluate current patterns (direct os.Getenv calls, dev/prod switches) and recommend a central config struct + validation strategy.

Entry points:
- go-backend/main.go:36-77, 233-247
acceptance_criteria: - List of env vars + where used\n- Recommendation for config structure + validation (fail-fast vs defaults)\n- Proposed file/module placement (e.g., bootstrap/config.go)
notes:
## Review notes: configuration + env var management

### 1) Inventory of env vars (name → purpose → where read)

**Runtime mode / logging**
- `ZETTEL_DEV` → dev/prod switch controlling log-to-file behavior → `go-backend/main.go:37`
- `ZETTEL_BACKEND_LOG_LOCATION` → file path for backend log output when not dev → `go-backend/main.go:38`
- `ZETTEL_DEBUG` → enables per-route request logging → `go-backend/handlers/log.go:19`
- `ZETTEL_IS_TESTING` → skips Typesense operations in services layer → `go-backend/services/typesense.go:15`, `go-backend/services/typesense.go:62`

**HTTP / frontend URL / CORS / redirects**
- `ZETTEL_PORT` → backend listen port (default `8080`) → `go-backend/main.go:244-247`
- `ZETTEL_URL` → frontend origin used for CORS + redirects + password reset URLs → `go-backend/main.go:234`, `go-backend/handlers/oauth.go:149`, `go-backend/handlers/auth.go:309`, `go-backend/handlers/billing.go:93-95`

**Database**
- `DB_HOST` / `DB_PORT` / `DB_USER` / `DB_PASS` / `DB_NAME` → DB connection parameters → `go-backend/bootstrap/bootstrap.go:13-17` (also in scripts/tests: `go-backend/scripts/*`, `go-backend/tests/conftest.go:33-36`)

**JWT / auth**
- `SECRET_KEY` → JWT signing secret → `go-backend/main.go:74`

**Mail**
- `MAIL_HOST` / `MAIL_PASSWORD` → mail service configuration → `go-backend/main.go:59-60`, `go-backend/cmd/reminders/main.go:17-18`

**S3 / Backblaze B2**
- `B2_BUCKET_NAME` → bucket name (currently read at package init) → `go-backend/handlers/s3.go:19`
- `B2_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `B2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` → B2 credentials → `go-backend/handlers/s3.go:23-28`

**Typesense**
- `TYPESENSE_HOST` / `TYPESENSE_PASSWORD` → Typesense server + API key → `go-backend/bootstrap/typesense.go:14-16`
- `TYPESENSE_COLLECTION` → collection name → `go-backend/bootstrap/typesense.go:26` (also used throughout handlers/services e.g. `go-backend/services/typesense.go:31-32`, `go-backend/handlers/search.go:37`)

**Stripe**
- `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` → Stripe API key (global stripe-go) → `go-backend/main.go:54`
- `STRIPE_MONTH_PRICE` / `STRIPE_YEAR_PRICE` → Price IDs for subscription plans → `go-backend/handlers/billing.go:81-83`
- `STRIPE_BILLING_URL` → billing portal URL → `go-backend/handlers/billing.go:125-126`
- `STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` → frontend public key → `go-backend/handlers/billing.go:136-137`
- `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → webhook signature verification → `go-backend/handlers/billing.go:164-166`
- `ZETTEL_ADMIN_EMAIL` → admin notification recipient → `go-backend/handlers/billing.go:148-150`

**GitHub OAuth**
- `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` / `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` / `GITHUB_REDIRECT_URI` → GitHub OAuth config → `go-backend/handlers/oauth.go:26-28`, `go-backend/handlers/oauth.go:45-48`

**LLM / OpenAI-compatible**
- `ZETTEL_LLM_KEY` / `ZETTEL_LLM_ENDPOINT` → client auth + base URL → `go-backend/main.go:75-76`, `go-backend/services/llms.go:15-17`
- `ZETTEL_LLM_DEFAULT_MODEL` → default model name → `go-backend/services/llms.go:18-19`
- `ZETTEL_LLM_SUMMARIZE_MODEL` → summarize model name → `go-backend/services/summarize.go:179`
- `ZETTEL_RUN_CHUNKING_EMBEDDING` → controls background chunking/embedding job → `go-backend/main.go:78`

---

### 2) Pain points / risks (with file pointers)

**Config is scattered and untyped**
- Direct `os.Getenv` usage is spread across `main.go`, `bootstrap`, `handlers`, and `services`, which makes it difficult to see required vs optional config and to test reliably.
  - Examples: `go-backend/main.go:37-78`, `go-backend/bootstrap/bootstrap.go:12-23`, `go-backend/handlers/billing.go:80-96`, `go-backend/services/llms.go:15-19`.

**Secrets potentially logged**
- `main.go` logs the `MailClient` struct via `%v` (`log.Printf("email server: %v", s.Mail)`). Since `MailClient` contains `Password`, this likely prints `MAIL_PASSWORD` into logs.
  - `go-backend/main.go:58-63` (password field is set) + `go-backend/main.go:73` (logged).

**Env reads at package init time**
- `bucketName` is read as a package-level var. This happens during import/init, not during explicit startup, which complicates tests and makes missing env vars fail later and less predictably.
  - `go-backend/handlers/s3.go:19`.

**Inconsistent validation / defaults**
- Some values have defaults (`ZETTEL_PORT` → `8080` in `go-backend/main.go:244-247`), some fail fast (`B2_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `B2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` in `go-backend/handlers/s3.go:26-28`), and many are implicitly “required” but not validated early (e.g. `SECRET_KEY` at `go-backend/main.go:74`, `ZETTEL_URL` at `go-backend/main.go:234`).

**Testing behavior is controlled via env in deeper layers**
- Typesense writes are disabled via `ZETTEL_IS_TESTING` checks inside services (`go-backend/services/typesense.go:14-16`, `go-backend/services/typesense.go:61-63`) rather than being driven by a single test-mode flag on the server/config.

**Duplication / drift risk for LLM config**
- `main.go` creates an OpenAI config (`go-backend/main.go:75-76`) but doesn’t appear to use it; `services/llms.go` constructs the client from env again (`go-backend/services/llms.go:15-19`). This invites confusion about the “source of truth”.

---

### 3) Suggested refactor steps (small + incremental, refactor-only)

These align with follow-up bead `Zettelgarden-9xw.9`.

1. **Introduce a single config module**
   - Add `go-backend/config` (or `go-backend/bootstrap/config.go`) with a `Config` struct and `LoadFromEnv() (Config, error)`.
   - Parse/validate types once: booleans (`ZETTEL_DEV`, `ZETTEL_DEBUG`, `ZETTEL_IS_TESTING`), ints (`ZETTEL_PORT`), required strings.

2. **Make required vs optional explicit**
   - Fail fast (startup) for true requirements: DB params, `SECRET_KEY`, `ZETTEL_URL` (if needed for OAuth/CORS), Stripe keys (if billing enabled), etc.
   - Keep existing defaults where already present (e.g. `ZETTEL_PORT` default `8080`).

3. **Add redaction-safe logging**
   - Ensure config structs (mail, stripe, etc.) are not logged directly, or implement a redacted stringer for config types.
   - Immediate follow-up candidate: remove the `MailClient` log line or make it safe.

4. **Thread config into init points (don’t read env in leaf packages)**
   - `bootstrap.InitServer(cfg)` should accept a `DatabaseConfig` rather than calling `os.Getenv` itself.
   - `bootstrap.InitTypesense(cfg)` should accept Typesense host/API key/collection.
   - `Handler.CreateS3Client(cfg)` should accept bucket name + credentials and avoid package-level env reads.

5. **Unify “testing” behavior**
   - Replace `ZETTEL_IS_TESTING` checks in service code with a server/config-level `Testing` boolean.

---

### 4) Candidate follow-up beads

**Already tracked**
- `Zettelgarden-9xw.9` (P1): centralize config loading (Config struct + validation). Recommend splitting into sub-steps internally (config struct first, then replace env reads in main/bootstrap, then leaf packages).

**New candidates**
- (New) “Follow-up: stop logging sensitive config structs”
  - Acceptance: no logs print secrets (mail password, JWT secret, API keys). Add/verify redaction.
- (New) “Follow-up: eliminate env-driven test toggles in service layer”
  - Acceptance: `ZETTEL_IS_TESTING` is not read in services; test mode is driven by server/config injection.

title: Deleted cards continue to appear in Typesense search index
description:
Bug: Deleted cards (marked with is_deleted = TRUE) continue to show up in search results because the Typesense index initialization queries don't filter out deleted cards.

**Root Cause:**
The InitSearchCollection() function in handlers/search.go has two queries that don't filter out deleted cards:
1. Cards query (lines 40-55): SELECT all cards without filtering is_deleted
2. Facts query (lines 127-133): JOIN cards without filtering is_deleted

**Impact:**
When Typesense index is rebuilt or populated initially, deleted cards get included because the source queries grab ALL cards from the database.

**Current Deletion Logic is Correct:**
The actual deletion process WORKS - deleted cards ARE removed from Typesense via deleteCardTypesense() call. The problem is only with initial population.

**Fix Needed:**
Add WHERE clauses to both queries:
- Cards query: AND c.is_deleted = FALSE
- Facts query: AND c.is_deleted = FALSE

**Files to Change:**
- go-backend/handlers/search.go: lines 40-55 and 127-133

**Similar Fix Reference:**
Commit 4a8751b fixed a similar issue in GetChildCards() by adding is_deleted = FALSE filter.

title: Tasks: quick #tag entry in task dialogs
description:
Add an inline quick-tag entry UX so users can type '#' in task create/edit flows and get a small autocomplete window to insert existing tags (and optionally create a new tag).

Scope:
- Visible in both CreateTaskWindow and TaskDialog task editing surfaces.
- Reuse existing tag source (TaskContext allTags) and existing tag parsing/append logic (utils/tasks.parseTags + TaskForm tag handlers).

UX requirements:
- When cursor is in the task title input and the user types '#', open a small popover anchored to the caret/field.
- As user continues typing after '#', filter existing tags by prefix (case-insensitive).
- Keyboard: ArrowUp/ArrowDown to navigate, Enter to select, Escape to close.
- Selecting a tag inserts it as '#tag' in the title (space-delimited), without duplicating existing tags.
- Mouse: clicking a suggestion inserts it.
- Close popover when selection made, on Escape, or when the user leaves the hashtag context (space/newline).

Non-goals:
- No backend changes. Tags remain represented via hashtags in title + Task.tags array as today.

Acceptance criteria:
- In CreateTaskWindow and TaskDialog, typing '#wor' shows suggestions like '#work' (from existing tags).
- Selecting a suggestion results in a correctly formatted hashtag in the task title.
- No duplicate hashtags are inserted.
- Works in create (local state) and edit (saveOnChange) modes without breaking existing tag editor.
